meta.guide_tau: Level caption:  energy (NIST, or a measurement of the last 20 years where one exists) and measured lifetime (where one exists).
meta.notes: Isotope shifts are nu(first)-nu(second) as in the schema; where a source tabulated nu(A)-nu(164) the sign was flipped and this is stated in the entry note. Keys other than 164-x (e.g. 162-164 for Petersen et al., 163-162 for White et al.) are kept as printed. Extra fields beyond SCHEMA.md are used where the schema had no slot: top-level ionization_limit; level fields lifetime_other, hyperfine_other, level_energy_measured; transition fields linewidth_MHz / linewidth_kHz, wavenumber_cm, reduced_dipole_au (|<f||D||i>| in atomic units, theory), leak_to_metastable, isotope_shift_other, frequency_other, polarizability_ratio_1064nm, note. Entries flagged LOWER LIMIT / UPPER LIMIT / LOWER BOUND in their note are bounds, not central values. g_J values are copied from the NIST levels file (Lande column). Hyperfine A, B follow the usual convention E = A K/2 + B [3K(K+1)/4 - I(I+1)J(J+1)] / [2I(2I-1)J(2J-1)], K = F(F+1)-I(I+1)-J(J+1); 161Dy has negative A (inverted structure). The Curry 1997 and Gustavsson 1979 lifetime tables were read from the publisher HTML pages through an automated page reader (direct download is captcha-blocked), not from a PDF; the Curry values were spot-checked against 1/sum(A) from the NIST lines file for 15194.83, 15972.35, 16693.87, 16733.20, 23832.06, 23877.74 and 24708.97 cm-1 and agree. Curry uncertainties are the blanket +-5% (+-10% or +-8% where flagged). Rows of Curry Table 1 above 28200 cm-1 were not transcribed, and levels the reader may have skipped are simply absent. CONFLICTS: (1) "598/599 nm, 12 kHz": Lu et al. 2011 and the Lu thesis assign 12 kHz (theory) to the closed J=8->9 line to 4f9 5d6s2 7K9 at 16717.79 cm-1 (598.2 nm vac); Chakravarthy et al. 2025 attach "tau = 13 us, 12 kHz" to the 599 nm J=8->7 line to 16693.87 cm-1 (598.856 nm air), but that level has a measured lifetime of 1.78 us (Curry) / 1.90(7) us (Gustavsson) and NIST A = 5.6e5 s^-1, i.e. about 89 kHz. (2) 626 nm: 136(4) kHz (Gustavsson lifetime 1170(30) ns) and 135 kHz / 8.5e5 s^-1 (Lu et al.) versus NIST A = 8.9e5 s^-1 (Curry lifetime 1120 ns, 142 kHz). (3) 421 nm: 31.9(8) MHz (Lu et al.), 32.2 MHz used by Stuttgart/Innsbruck, Curry 4.8 ns = 33.1(17) MHz, NIST A = 2.08e8 s^-1. (4) 1001 nm: measured lifetime >= 87.2(6.7) ms versus theory 3 ms; the 2.9(1) us value of Studer et al. is an oven-collision-limited lower bound. Level energy 9991.004(1) cm-1 (164Dy, Studer) versus 9990.9666(10) cm-1 (162Dy, Petersen) differ by the isotope shift. (5) 741 nm lifetime 89.3(8) us versus theory 21 us; Studer et al. label the line A = 1.16e4 Hz in a figure versus 1.12e4 s^-1 from Lu et al. (6) Ground-state 163Dy B: 1152.869(40) MHz (Childs 1970 via White et al.) versus 1153.8684 MHz (Ferch 1974 via Maier thesis). (7) 421 nm leak: measured B ~ 7e-6 (MOT), theory (6+-3)e-5 as an upper estimate, beam bound < 5e-4. (8) Ionization limit 47901.76(5) cm-1 (NIST) versus 47901.8265(8) cm-1 (162Dy, Ferioli et al. 2026). (9) 741 nm 164-162 isotope shift 1214(3) MHz (Lu) versus 1245(32) MHz (Studer), consistent within errors. (10) Dzuba & Flambaum Table III lists a 421-level decay channel to a J=9 level at 23218 cm-1 with amplitude 0.0076 a.u. and probability 0.846E+03 s^-1, which are mutually inconsistent (omega = 518 cm-1); that channel is omitted. Ng et al. 2026 and Li et al. 2017 both argue the J=9 level at 27014.02 cm-1 (370.18 nm line) does not connect to the ground state. Dy tweezer imaging on 626 nm (Bloch et al. 2023, arXiv:2307.04689): atoms are pumped to metastable states by trap-light two-photon processes, about 65% of those decays go to trapped metastable states, return time 0.48(8) s; states unidentified.
